title: Sparrow Template Studio — personal scratchbook
content:
Purpose:
Small personal scratchbook for iterating on small template families and few-shot sets. Goal is to surface compact, reusable building blocks (Sparrow-family) for user-facing completions and for routing to cheaper model variants. Not a final library; this is intentionally messy and experimental.

High-level hypotheses:
- Short, conversational priming + 1–2 exemplars beats long instruction blocks for fine-grained tone control in multi-turn UIs.
- Anchoring a single, concrete example (instead of 3 varied ones) helps with hallucination on structured output tasks (fields, JSON).
- Fewer tokens + targeted system instructions are cheaper and often as reliable if we pair with a local reranker/validator.

Template inventory (sketches):
1) Sparrow-compact: system: "You are a concise assistant that returns bullet answers. Keep to 2–4 bullets." user: "Summarize: <<text>>"
   - Variant A: add explicit token budget: "Answer in under 60 tokens."
   - Variant B: soft style: "Use friendly, non-technical language."

2) Sparrow-struct: system: "Return strictly valid JSON with keys: summary, confidence, actions. No extra text." user: "Analyze this note: <<text>>"
   - Add exemplar where summary: short, confidence: 0.88, actions: [..]

3) Sparrow-roleplay-lite: one-line persona marker + one-shot: "You are an onboarding coach. Example Q->A (user: 'How do I connect my API key?' -> assistant: stepwise)."

Few-shot sets (mini experiments):
- FS-quick-2: two exemplars (positive/negative) for classification into {support, billing, product}. Use headings only.
- FS-json-1: one exemplar of correct JSON output and one malformed example; see whether model self-corrects after validator feedback.
- FS-tone-3: three exemplars for tone calibration (formal, neutral, playful) but keep them extremely short.

Failure matrix (observed failure modes + quick remedies):
- Failure: extra prose outside JSON in Sparrow-struct.
  Symptoms: trailing sentence like "Hope this helps".
  Quick fix: tighten system message + post-check filter that strips non-JSON and asks for regeneration once.

- Failure: model repeats exemplar verbatim for paraphrase tasks.
  Symptoms: high overlap with provided example, low novelty.
  Fix ideas: randomize exemplar tokens slightly, or use negative exemplar showing what *not* to do.

- Failure: tone drift after 2nd turn in roleplay-lite.
  Symptoms: assistant slowly moves from persona to generic help.
  Fix: re-insert the one-line persona at each turn, or include a short anchoring token sequence ("[SPARROW_PERSONA]").

Quick experiments (notes and tiny logs):
- 2024-09-20: Sparrow-compact + Variant A against gpt-3-style baseline. Observed: 18% token savings, equal user-perceived quality on our internal micro-eval of 120 prompts.
- 2024-10-02: FS-json-1 on smaller quantized model (4-bit) -> 42% of responses valid JSON vs 61% on unquantized. Post-filter + single retry improved to 78%.
- 2024-11-15: Roleplay-lite with persona marker re-sent each turn reduced tone drift by ~60% in 50-dialogue test.

Open questions / TODOs (to self):
- Should we prefer 1 exemplar + explicit rubric vs 3 exemplars without rubric for structured outputs? Quick AB on 200 items.
- Test Sparrow-struct + sample-temperature scheduling (low temp for keys, higher for freeform fields).
- Build a tiny validation harness: run on cheap model, if fails, call fallback model and log reasons. Keep minimal costs.
- Split format: add short-hand anchors for common customer intents (login, billing, integration, feature-request).

Notes to self (messy):
- Try mixing negative exemplar ("Bad output: ...") — I think model learns to avoid that space.
- Watch for token explosion when adding confidence fields — maybe compress float to one decimal.
- Keep system messages short-ish (<=20 tokens) when targeting latency-sensitive endpoints.

References and links (working list):
- Slack thread: #devex-prompt-bench (see thread ts: 2024-10-05)
- GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sparrow-experiments/pull/12 (current code to run FS-quick-2)
- JIRA: DEVEX-241 (validation harness spike)

Mini changelog:
- 2024-09-18: initial sketch.
- 2024-10-03: added compact variant notes and FS results.
- 2024-11-20: logged roleplay-lite drift analysis.
- 2025-02-03: updated failure matrix with new mitigation (post-filter + retry).

End of scratchbook — returning to clean up into a proper Prompt Library entry once I have clearer AB results.

---
Small reminder: this file is mine for iterative thinking; move only the stable templates into the shared library (confluence/PromptLibrary) after review.
